skill.name: when-validating-code-works-use-functionality-audit
skill.description: Guides runtime functionality audits for generated or modified code. It covers sandbox setup, test execution, debugging, regression checks, and audit reporting.
skill.summary: Validate code behavior through sandboxed test execution and structured debugging.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, Graphviz labels, local test imports, and dummy environment examples. The confirmed risks are operational: the skill runs external commands, installs dependencies, mounts workspaces into Docker, deletes a fixed temporary directory, and stores audit artifacts in shared memory. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before installing dependencies or running tests. Prefer containers or virtual machines with read-only source mounts, network limits, and disabled package lifecycle scripts.

remediation.issue: Persistent storage of logs and reports
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets, tokens, customer data, and stack traces before storing logs, reports, or metrics in Claude Flow memory.
Use mktemp -d, quote command substitutions, validate sandbox paths, and avoid fixed rm -rf cleanup paths.
Pin package versions and document npm and pip lifecycle script risks before users run install commands.

content.user_title: Validate Code Functionality With Runtime Audits
content.value_statement: Code can look complete while failing at runtime. This skill guides sandbox setup, test execution, debugging, regression checks, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of isolated temporary test workspaces.
Runs unit, integration, and edge-case test scenarios.
Captures test logs, coverage metrics, and exit codes.
Categorizes failures into syntax, runtime, logic, dependency, and integration issues.
Reruns tests after fixes to check regressions and readiness.
Produces Markdown reports and metrics artifacts.
limitations: Requires local test tooling and dependencies to be available or installable.
Can execute project code and package scripts, so untrusted projects need stronger isolation.
Examples focus mainly on Node.js, Jest, and pytest workflows.
Does not replace human review for security or product correctness.

output_examples.input: Validate an authentication module after generated changes.
output: Unit tests passed, but two integration checks failed on token refresh behavior.
Recommended fix: update refresh handling and rerun the authentication regression suite.

output_examples.input: Check a data processing function before merge.
output: Happy-path, missing-field, and invalid-format cases passed.
Coverage improved, and no regressions were detected in related tests.

output_examples.input: Review deployment readiness for a service change.
output: The service passed local unit tests but failed one production readiness gate.
Recommended action: resolve the failing health-check scenario before deployment.

best_practices: Run audits in disposable workspaces with only the files needed for validation.
Record commands, exit codes, logs, and coverage so results can be reproduced.
Rerun previously passing tests after each fix to catch regressions early.
anti_patterns: Running untrusted projects on the host without isolation or confirmation.
Accepting generated tests that only assert placeholder success.
Reporting readiness without rerunning tests after fixes.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps verify that code works at runtime instead of relying only on static review or visual inspection.

faq.question: Does it write or run files?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes creating test artifacts, installing dependencies, and running tests in a temporary workspace.

faq.question: Can it validate third-party code?
faq.answer: Yes, but third-party code should run in stronger isolation because tests and package scripts can execute arbitrary commands.

faq.question: Which stacks are covered best?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Node.js, Jest, TypeScript, and pytest, with room to adapt to other test frameworks.

faq.question: Does it replace CI pipelines?
faq.answer: No. It complements CI by guiding local or agent-assisted audits and producing evidence for later automation.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review dependency installs, test commands, Docker mounts, and any logs stored outside the sandbox.
